content: 1. Hormonal contraceptives may have reduced efficacy when used with certain medications. It is recommended to use non-hormonal contraceptive methods as an alternative. 2. Dexlansoprazole can decrease the effectiveness of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of diazepam by reducing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to higher serum concentrations. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Dicloxacillin may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Didanosine can decrease the effectiveness of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Didanosine should be administered two hours before or several hours after ferrous fumarate. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Ferrous fumarate can reduce the effectiveness of dolutegravir by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Dolutegravir should be administered two hours before or six hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the serum concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) such as dosulepin and doxepin by reducing their oxidative metabolism. This can lead to increased antidepressant effects and potential adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 8. Doxycycline may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Ferrous fumarate can decrease the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs or avoidance of co-administration is recommended. 10. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 11. Efavirenz can reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may have reduced efficacy, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Elafibranor, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the systemic exposure of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptives or barrier methods should be used during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. 13. Elagolix, a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, can reduce the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 14. Ethinyl estradiol may reduce the efficacy of elagolix due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptives are advised. 15. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Ferrous fumarate can decrease eltrombopag levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration should be avoided, and a four-hour separation is recommended. 16. Elvitegravir may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be considered. 17. Enasidenib may alter the concentrations of combined hormonal contraceptives. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Co-administration with sensitive substrates of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP should be avoided. 18. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentrations and toxicities of BCRP substrates. It may also reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 19. Ethinyl estradiol may reduce the effects of enoxaparin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Enzalutamide can reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during co-administration, and non-hormonal methods are recommended. 21. Erythromycin derivatives may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Eslicarbazepine acetate can reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 23. Esomeprazole can decrease the effectiveness of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Exenatide may impair the absorption of oral contraceptives by slowing gastric emptying. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. 25. Famotidine can decrease the effectiveness of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Fedratinib may increase the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 27. Felbamate may reduce the levels of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of adverse effects. 29. Fluconazole can increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 30. Fluvoxamine can increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Fosphenytoin can reduce the effectiveness of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during co-administration, and non-hormonal methods are recommended.
